Indication: Left knee MRI [DATE]
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. [REDACTED]. Moderate reciprocal osseous stress in the medial tibial plateau. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex degenerative tearing and maceration extending from the posterior horn to the body of the medial meniscus with severe extrusion.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	[REDACTED]. Moderate reciprocal osseous stress in the medial tibial plateau.
2.	Severe medial compartment osteoarthritis with complex degenerative tearing of the medial meniscus, similar to prior study.
3.	Mild patellofemoral chondrosis.
4.	Moderate knee effusion.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: One month of knee pain.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Focal subchondral marrow edema at the anterior peripheral margin of the medial tibial plateau. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Moderate, multiloculated Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: High-grade radial tear of the posterior root with moderate peripheral extrusion and superimposed complex tearing of the body and posterior horn.
Medial compartment cartilage: Large areas of full-thickness chondrosis along the weightbearing femoral condyle with underlying subchondral cystic change/edema. Diffuse high-grade tibial cartilage loss with full-thickness loss at the peripheral margin.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the femoral condyle and tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full-thickness cartilage loss along the superior aspect of the medial patellar facet with underlying subchondral cystic change and edema. Diffuse thinning of the trochlear cartilage, without focal defect.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Intact, with thickening of the proximal ligament suggestive of prior injury. Bowed morphology and periligamentous edema likely secondary to meniscal extrusion.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: Mild patellar tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 13 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Moderate to severe medial compartment osteoarthritis with complex meniscal tearing and reactive subchondral edema at the peripheral medial tibial plateau.

MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    Clicking, locking, exclude meniscal tear..

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination. The extensor mechanism is intact. There is patella alta. The Insall Salvati ratio measures about 1.6.
The finding is associated with advanced patellofemoral joint osteoarthritic change with extensive denuding of the articular cartilage and with extensive subcortical cyst formation particularly seen along the apex and lateral facet of patella. Prominent trochlear and patellar osteophytes are demonstrated.

The medial patellar retinaculum is attenuated likely related to previous lateral dislocation and partial disruption. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact.

There is a degenerative medial meniscal tear. There is maceration and linear signal seen in the posterior horn extending into the body. An oblique inferiorly surfacing tear of the body and posterior horn is a demonstrated. The finding is associated with severe chondral denuding and exuberant marginal osteophyte formation seen to the medial joint compartment. There is also subcortical edema seen to the weightbearing surface of the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau.

The lateral meniscus is macerated and not identified at the body and posterior horn. Findings are in keeping with extensive maceration and degenerative tearing of the body and the posterior horn of lateral meniscus. The finding is associated with denuding of the entire articular cartilage of lateral joint compartment associated with prominent lateral joint compartment osteophyte formation. There is also subcortical sclerosis and mild edema seen within the lateral joint compartment. An intraosseous cyst is seen to the lateral femoral condyle with 3 cm in keeping with subcortical tear.

The anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate and medial collateral ligament are intact.

The lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon appear intact.

There is a large knee effusion with reactive synovitis. There is no significant Baker's cyst. In the lateral popliteal fossa there is a large intraosseous loose body projecting anterior to the proximal fibers of the lateral head of the gastrocnemius measuring about 2.4 cm in maximum dimension. Smaller loose bodies are likely present in this region.

INTERPRETATION: 

Severe tricompartmental osteoarthritic change most severely affecting patellofemoral and lateral compartments. Degenerative meniscal tears laterally and medially with cartilaginous denuding to the lateral medial and patellofemoral compartments.

Loose bodies.

Patella alta with attenuation of the medial patellar retinaculum likely related to prior transient lateral dislocation of the patella.

MRI  KNEE  -  RIGHT

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multiplanar multisequence MR images of the knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Suspected large and destructive meniscal tear hindering mobility.

COMPARISON:  Knee x-rays [Date].

FINDINGS:

Medial meniscus: Oblique tear of the posterior medial meniscus with inferior articular surfacing. Incidental meniscal flounce.

Medial compartment articular cartilage:  Grade 2 chondrosis with mild degenerative changes, including osteophyte formation.

MCL:  Mild thickening, consistent with chronic sprain.

Lateral meniscus: The lateral meniscus is peripherally extruded and macerated, consistent with extensive complex degenerative tear. 

Lateral compartment articular cartilage:  Grade 4 chondrosis with complete denuding of the articular surface and extensive degenerative changes, including bone-on-bone articulation, subchondral edema and cystic change, and osteophyte formation.

LCL complex:  Intact.

ACL:  Intact.

PCL:  Intact.

Quadriceps and patellar tendons:  Intact.

Patellofemoral alignment: Normal.

Patellofemoral cartilage:  Grade 1 chondrosis with mild degenerative changes.

Joint effusion:  Small volume effusion mostly in the suprapatellar recess.

Intra-articular bodies:  0.3 x 1.1 cm mineralized body in the posterior joint space.

Bone marrow:  Subchondral edema involving the lateral tibial plateau and lateral femoral condyle.

Popliteal fossa:  Normal.

Other findings:  Mild subcutaneous edema mostly over the lateral aspect of the knee. Fatty atrophy of the medial gastrocnemius muscle.


INTERPRETATION:

The lateral compartment is completely attenuated with bone-on-bone articulation and extensive degenerative changes. The lateral meniscus is nearly completely extruded and macerated, consistent with with an extensive complex degenerative tear.

Oblique tear of the posterior medial meniscus with inferior articular surfacing. 

Mild patellofemoral and medial compartment degenerative changes. Small joint effusion.

The extensor mechanism, LCL complex, MCL, ACL, and PCL are intact.

Indication: [REDACTED].
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Full-thickness chondrosis at the proximal tibiofibular joint with marginal osteophytes and subchondral cystic change and intra-osseous ganglion cyst formation. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Tricompartmental marginal osteophytes.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion with synovitis. No intra-articular bodies. Small multilobulated Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Extensive complex tear at the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus with maceration and extrusion. Reactive edema at the joint line.
Medial compartment cartilage: Full thickness cartilage denudation throughout the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau with subchondral cystic change and marrow edema.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss at the anterior weightbearing surfaces. High grade chondrosis along the peripheral lateral joint. 

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss along the medial trochlea. High-grade fissuring at the median ridge with likely an early delaminating component extending along the medial patellar facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal fibers with bowing related to medial meniscus extrusion.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Mild popliteus tendonesis without tear. Ganglion cyst about the myotendinous junction. 

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: Mild proximal patellar tendinosis without tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 4 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Extensive complex tear at the body and posterior horn of medial meniscus with maceration and extrusion of the body.
2.	Tricompartmental chondrosis, severe in the medial compartment. 
3.	Mild proximal patellar tendinosis without tear.
4.	Mild popliteus tendonesis without tear.
